picks.name: CoreMark (EEMBC), using the wasm3/wasm-coremark minimal port
picks.what: EEMBC CPU benchmark with linked-list, matrix, state-machine and CRC kernels. The kernels check their own results by comparing CRCs. License: the CoreMark acceptable-use agreement followed by Apache-2.0.
picks.size: About 2.2k lines. The 5 core .c files total 1,975 lines (core_list_join 595, core_main 442, core_matrix 359, core_state 330, core_util 249), coremark.h adds 183, and the port layer is core_portme.{c,h}.
picks.why_good: It is the CPU benchmark wasm runtimes use most. Its results are deterministic and CRC-validated across pointer chasing, integer matrix math, a switch-based state machine and CRC bit operations, so it is the ideal first native-vs-MSIL comparison at -O0 and -O2.
picks.blockers:
Verified: a single TU set up as below compiles through the MSIL backend at -O0 and -O2 with no P/Invokes. It has not been run.
(1) coremark.h has no include guard, so #including the five core_*.c files fails with 'redefinition of list_data_s' (coremark.h:91). Put a copy of coremark.h with #pragma once next to the core files. An -I shadow header does not work, because quoted includes search the including file's directory first.
(2) ee_printf. The minimal port declares a variadic ee_printf in core_portme.h:183 and defines a variadic stub at core_portme.c:93. Upstream barebones instead defines a full printf in barebones/ee_printf.c. Callers are core_main.c (about 40 calls), core_util.c, core_list_join.c, core_matrix.c and core_state.c. Delete the declaration and the stub, then add '#define ee_printf(...) ((void)0)'. If the macro comes before the declaration, the declaration expands to 'int ((void)0);'.
(3) Do not reuse the wasm32 port's 'typedef ee_u32 ee_ptr_int'. MSIL pointers are 64-bit, so align_mem would truncate them and check_data_types would count an error. Use size_t or uintptr_t.
(4) MAIN_RETURN_VAL is the constant 0. #undef it after coremark.h and redefine it as (total_errors != 0) before including core_main.c, or patch core_main.c the way wasm-coremark does.
(5) Port settings: MEM_METHOD=MEM_STATIC (MEM_STACK puts the 2000-byte buffer in a localloc frame, and MEM_STATIC #errors if MULTITHREAD>1), MULTITHREAD=1, HAS_PRINTF=0, HAS_STDIO=0 (only the port files read HAS_TIME_H) and a fixed ITERATIONS. Stub start_time/stop_time/get_time with a fake clock that reports at least 10 seconds (11 s was used), because core_main.c adds to total_errors for shorter runs.
picks.tests: Self-validating against CRC tables indexed by known_id. 2K performance run (seeds 0,0,0x66; seedcrc 0xe9f5): list 0xe714, matrix 0x1fd7, state 0x8e3a. 2K validation run (seeds 0x3415,0x3415,0x66; seedcrc 0x18f2): list 0xe3c1, matrix 0x0747, state 0x8d84. crcfinal is not checked against any table. Upstream prints 'Correct operation validated' when total_errors==0. With ee_printf compiled out nothing prints, so report total_errors through the exit code.
picks.wasm_precedent: wasm3/wasm-coremark. Its minimal port has a single import, env.clock_ms (checked in the source and README, not in a built .wasm), and it patches core_main.c to export the score. Emscripten's test_benchmark.py also runs coremark. Listed but not verified: wasmer.io vshymanskyy/coremark, ncruces/wazero-coremark, WAMR tests/benchmarks/coremark.
claims_to_verify: running the compiled TU on .NET reproduces the 2K CRCs at -O0 and -O2 (compilation is verified, execution is not)
the wasmer.io, wazero and WAMR CoreMark ports exist

picks.name: Monocypher
picks.what: Small audited crypto library: XChaCha20-Poly1305, BLAKE2b, Argon2, X25519, EdDSA, Elligator. License: BSD-2-Clause or CC0-1.0.
picks.size: monocypher.c is 2,997 lines plus monocypher.h. The optional src/optional/monocypher-ed25519.c adds 503 lines (SHA-512/Ed25519).
picks.why_good: Needs no libc or malloc. It is dense 64-bit integer code (field arithmetic with i64 multiplies and carries, rotates, constant-time selects) with no __int128, intrinsics or asm, and its known-answer vectors make the output exact.
picks.blockers:
The library needs nothing. Verified: monocypher.c's only #include is monocypher.h, which includes stddef.h and stdint.h. The -O2 IR on msvc-msil declares only LLVM intrinsics, and a full -S through the MSIL backend on linux-msil succeeds.
The upstream test driver needs more than a new reporter. tests/test.c has 48 printf calls and uses memcpy/memset/free. In tests/utils.c, alloc() calls malloc, vector_test() uses memcmp/free/printf and vector_of_string() uses strlen. In tests/utils.h, ASSERT uses fprintf(stderr) and exit.
For Phase 1, #include test.c and utils.c into one TU and supply:
- an arena alloc() with a no-op free
- a local strlen and memcmp
- a puts-based ASSERT
- a reporter that uses puts or the exit code
tests/vectors.h is generated with libsodium, so take it from a release tarball (4.0.2 ships it). Alternatively use the smaller tests/tis-ci.c driver with the checked-in tests/tis-ci-vectors.h (474+532 lines), which has the same libc needs. Give Argon2 a static work area, because address-taken locals live in a localloc frame.
picks.tests: Known-answer vectors for every primitive (tests/test.c with vectors.h, or tests/tis-ci.c with tis-ci-vectors.h). Output is fully deterministic.
picks.wasm_precedent: ar-nelson/monocypher-wasm (deno.land/x/monocypher) compiles monocypher.c and wingo's walloc.c with 'clang -c' and links with 'wasm-ld --no-entry'. It tracks Monocypher 3.1.x, not 4.x.
claims_to_verify: the vectors pass when run on .NET (only compilation through the backend was verified)
the rewritten driver (test.c + utils.c with harness definitions) compiles in Phase 1 with no other libc references

picks.name: TweetNaCl
picks.what: NaCl crypto (crypto_box, secretbox, sign/Ed25519, SHA-512) in about 100 tweets of C. Public domain.
picks.size: tweetnacl.c is 809 lines and tweetnacl.h is 272 lines (mostly macros). One TU.
picks.why_good: Needs no libc, and its field arithmetic is i64-heavy. u32 is typedef'd to unsigned long, so it is 32-bit on x86_64-pc-windows-msvc-msil and 64-bit on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-msil while the output must stay the same, which makes it a direct cross-triple data-model check.
picks.blockers:
The harness must define 'void randombytes(u8 *, u64)'. tweetnacl.c:10 declares it extern, and crypto_box_keypair (line 452) and crypto_sign_keypair (line 662) reference it. Compiling tweetnacl.c alone on linux-msil therefore fails with "undefined function 'randombytes' is not defined in this module and is not a Phase-1 import". With a deterministic stub it compiles through the backend (verified).
There is no bundled test suite: the site ships only tweetnacl.c/.h, tweetnacl.h.py, the tweets and squeeze.py.
picks.tests: No bundled suite. Use NaCl/libsodium known-answer vectors, or diff outputs for fixed keys and nonces against a native build on both triples.
picks.wasm_precedent: Weak. tweetnacl-js is a hand port to JS, and no C-to-wasm build was verified.
claims_to_verify: output is identical on both triples. The 64-bit u32 argument comes from reading the code (L32 masks with 0xffffffff, st32 stores the low 4 bytes, the carries mask with &255 and &3); it was not run
a C-to-wasm build of tweetnacl.c exists

picks.name: BLAKE2 reference implementations (ref/: blake2b, blake2s, blake2bp, blake2sp)
picks.what: Official portable reference C code for the BLAKE2 hash family, with a built-in known-answer self-test. License: CC0, OpenSSL or Apache-2.0, at the user's choice.
picks.size: ref/blake2b-ref.c is 379 lines and blake2s-ref.c is similar. Add blake2.h, blake2-impl.h and testvectors/blake2-kat.h (the KAT table).
picks.why_good: The self-test already reports through puts, and the code exercises 64/32-bit rotates and little-endian loads. It also covers taking the address of a libc-named function: blake2-impl.h:154-158 stores &memset in a static const volatile function pointer and calls through it (ldftn plus calli).
picks.blockers:
Define memset and memcmp in the harness. memset's address is taken, so the intrinsic alone is not enough, and the self-test calls memcmp. The explicit import attribute is not an option from C today: clang's import_module/import_name are WebAssembly-only and are ignored with a warning on the MSIL triples.
Verified on x86_64-pc-windows-msvc-msil at -O2 -Wall with -DBLAKE2B_SELFTEST: no diagnostics. The IL has memset and memcmp methods, an ldftn of memset stored in secure_zero_memory's memset_v, and puts as pinvokeimpl("ucrtbase"). Without the two definitions the build fails with "undefined function 'memset'/'memcmp'".
There is no -Winconsistent-dllimport issue, because vcruntime_string.h declares memcmp/memcpy/memset without _VCRTIMP. The msil clang driver did not find the UCRT/MSVC headers by itself, so pass -isystem for both.
Add -I testvectors, because blake2-kat.h lives there (ref/makefile uses -I../testvectors). blake2bp/blake2sp need blake2b-ref.c/blake2s-ref.c in the same TU. Their OpenMP code is under #if _OPENMP.
picks.tests: -DBLAKE2B_SELFTEST (and the matching macros for the other variants) builds a main() that checks blake2-kat.h, prints 'ok' and returns 0 on success, and prints 'error' and returns -1 on failure. testvectors/ also has JSON vectors.
picks.wasm_precedent: Not verified: argon2-browser compiles the Argon2 reference C with Emscripten and bundles the BLAKE2b reference under src/blake2, and a blakejs 'emscripten' branch experiment compiled the BLAKE2 reference C to wasm.
claims_to_verify: the self-test prints 'ok' when run on .NET (compiled on msvc-msil, not run)
the linux-msil build against glibc headers (not tested; no glibc headers were installed)
the argon2-browser and blakejs wasm precedents

picks.name: jsmn
picks.what: Minimal C89 JSON tokenizer. It writes tokens into a caller-provided array and never allocates. MIT.
picks.size: jsmn.h is 471 lines. A single header.
picks.why_good: Zero libc. It is a pointer- and index-heavy character scanner with a switch, and the JSMN_PARENT_LINKS and JSMN_STRICT macros give four builds to cross-check, with token arrays that are easy to checksum.
picks.blockers:
None for the library. jsmn.h's only #include is stddef.h, and both the default build and the JSMN_STRICT+JSMN_PARENT_LINKS build compile through the MSIL backend with no declarations in the IR (verified).
The unit tests need real porting. In test/testutil.h, tokeq() and parse() are variadic definitions that read the expected tokens with va_arg. parse() also mallocs (and never frees) and uses strlen/strncmp, and failures print with printf %.*s. Turn each expected-token list into an array and report through puts.
picks.tests: test/tests.c with test/test.h and test/testutil.h. The Makefile builds test_default, test_strict, test_links and test_strict_links. Token output can also be compared with a native build over a corpus of JSON documents.
picks.wasm_precedent: None found for the C code; only a Rust port turned up.
claims_to_verify: the ported test cases pass on .NET (not run)

picks.name: yxml
picks.what: Small, fast streaming XML parser built as a generated state machine, with no malloc. MIT.
picks.size: yxml.c is about 1,060 lines, generated from the 313-line yxml.c.in by yxml-gen.pl and checked in. yxml.h adds 162 lines.
picks.why_good: Its large generated switch state machine stresses CIL 'switch' lowering and large CFGs. memset is its only libc call, and the caller supplies the buffer.
picks.blockers:
None for the library. yxml.c includes only yxml.h and string.h, memset (lines 275 and 325) becomes llvm.memset, and it compiles through the MSIL backend on msvc-msil (verified). Use the checked-in yxml.c, because regenerating it needs Perl.
The test driver test/test.c reads stdin with getc and uses printf, strlen and exit. A Phase 1 harness should embed each test .xml and its expected .out as strings and print the event stream with puts or putchar.
picks.tests: test/ has 43 .xml/.out pairs. test/test.sh runs './test < x.xml' for each and diffs the result against x.out.
picks.wasm_precedent: None found.
claims_to_verify: the embedded-test harness reproduces all 43 .out files on .NET (not run)

picks.name: tinf (tiny inflate)
picks.what: Tiny DEFLATE decompressor with zlib/gzip wrappers, Adler-32 and CRC-32. zlib license.
picks.size: src/*.c total 1,055 lines: tinflate.c (636) plus tinfzlib.c, tinfgzip.c, adler32.c and crc32.c. tinf.h adds 140.
picks.why_good: Needs no libc or malloc, and covers Huffman tree building, bit-level reading and table lookups. The zlib/gzip wrappers verify Adler-32/CRC-32, so decoding an embedded stream checks itself.
picks.blockers:
Compile with -DNDEBUG. Otherwise assert() references _wassert on msvc-msil (__assert_fail on glibc), which is not a Phase 1 import.
tinflate.c:60 and tinfgzip.c:36 both define 'static unsigned int read_le16', so a one-TU build fails with 'redefinition of read_le16'. Add '#define read_le16 gz_read_le16' before #including tinfgzip.c, or leave gzip out. With the rename and -DNDEBUG, all five files compile through the MSIL backend on msvc-msil (verified).
struct tinf_data (two 612-byte trees) is a local in tinf_uncompress, which is fine in a localloc frame.
picks.tests: test/ has CI tests (framework not checked). Decompress embedded zlib/gzip streams and check the wrapper checksums.
picks.wasm_precedent: None found.
claims_to_verify: decoding embedded streams on .NET passes the wrapper checksums (not run)
how the test/ suite is run

picks.name: LZ4 (lib/lz4.c block format)
picks.what: Extremely fast LZ77 block compressor and decompressor. lib/ is BSD-2-Clause.
picks.size: lib/lz4.c is 2,883 lines and lz4.h is 888 (HEAD 48bfbfe). lz4hc.c and lz4frame.c are optional.
picks.why_good: A hot integer loop with unaligned loads and stores through memcpy plus ctz/clz match-length counting. Its block output is byte-deterministic, so it round-trips and diffs against native.
picks.blockers:
-DLZ4_FREESTANDING=1 alone fails: lz4.h:112-124 #errors unless LZ4_memcpy, LZ4_memset and LZ4_memmove are also defined. Add -DLZ4_memcpy=__builtin_memcpy -DLZ4_memset=__builtin_memset -DLZ4_memmove=__builtin_memmove. The IR then has only llvm.memcpy/memset/memmove, and memmove lowers to Buffer.MemoryCopy. Freestanding mode also forces LZ4_HEAPMODE 0 and disables LZ4F and the heap APIs.
On x86_64-pc-windows-msvc-msil, _MSC_VER and _M_AMD64 make LZ4_NbCommonBytes call _tzcnt_u64, which fails as an undefined function. Add -DLZ4_FORCE_SW_BITCOUNT (verified). The linux-msil build compiles without it.
LZ4_compress_fast declares a 16,416-byte LZ4_stream_t local (at LZ4_MEMORY_USAGE 14), which becomes a localloc on the .NET stack. Use LZ4_compress_fast_extState with a static state, or lower LZ4_MEMORY_USAGE.
picks.tests: Upstream tests/ (fuzzer, frametest) use stdio. For Phase 1, round-trip embedded data and checksum the compressed bytes against a native build.
picks.wasm_precedent: wasm-lz4 (npm; cruise-automation/wasm-lz4) wraps upstream lz4 built with Emscripten SDK 2.0.23. It supports decompression only and was last updated in 2022. ukyo/lz4.js is reported to ship WASM and asm.js builds (not verified).
claims_to_verify: round-trip results on .NET match native (not run)
the ukyo/lz4.js wasm build

picks.name: LZAV
picks.what: Fast in-memory LZ77 compressor and decompressor in a single header. MIT.
picks.size: lzav.h is about 2,970 lines.
picks.why_good: On clang it uses __builtin_ctz/ctzll/clz/clzll/expect/prefetch, which exercises cttz/ctlz/prefetch lowering that few other picks reach. Its README claims WebAssembly compatibility, and round-trip output is deterministic.
picks.blockers:
Always define LZAV_MALLOC(s, T) and LZAV_FREE(p) together over a static arena; lzav.h:122-136 #errors if only one is defined.
Passing extbuf avoids the allocation only at run time. LZAV_FREE(alloc_buf) at line 1564 is unconditional, so with extbuf and no macro override the msvc-msil build fails at -O0 with undefined malloc and free. It passed at -O2 only because the branch was folded away. lzav_compress_hi always calls LZAV_MALLOC.
With arena macros, lzav_compress_default + lzav_compress_hi + lzav_decompress compile through the MSIL backend (verified).
Every compress call also puts an 8 KB 'uint32_t stack_buf[2048]' on the stack, which becomes a localloc frame. Otherwise it uses only memcpy/memset, which are intrinsics. (__builtin_bswap32 is used only on the big-endian path.)
picks.tests: No test suite in the repo. Round-trip plus a checksum compared with native.
picks.wasm_precedent: README.md:13 says the library is WebAssembly-compatible and runs at roughly half native speed against WASI libc. No named downstream wasm user was found.
claims_to_verify: round-trip results on .NET match native (not run)

picks.name: minimp3
picks.what: Minimalistic single-header MP1/MP2/MP3 decoder that passes the ISO conformance vectors. CC0-1.0.
picks.size: minimp3.h is 1,865 lines. minimp3_ex.h (1,436 lines) is not used.
picks.why_good: Real audio DSP: Huffman decoding, the IMDCT, polyphase synthesis and saturating float-to-int16 conversion, a mix of FP and integer code with large constant tables. The ISO conformance vectors come with reference PCM.
picks.blockers:
-DMINIMP3_NO_SIMD is required. Both MSIL triples predefine __x86_64__, __SSE__ and __SSE2__ (msvc also _M_X64 and _MSC_VER), so without it minimp3 selects immintrin.h, and the msvc-msil build fails with undefined _mm_loadu_ps, _mm_add_ps and the like. With it, minimp3.h compiles through the backend (verified).
Leave minimp3_ex.h out entirely: its realloc/malloc calls (lines 436, 450, 517, 682 and 1026) sit outside the MINIMP3_NO_STDIO guard. The core calls only memcpy/memset/memmove.
Make mp3dec_t static, embed one small vector and checksum the PCM. The default fp-contract on the msil triples produces llvm.fmuladd, so compile both sides with -ffp-contract=off for bit-exact PCM.
picks.tests: vectors/ has 83 .bit streams with 83 matching .pcm references; upstream requires PSNR above 96 dB. Phase 1 compares a PCM checksum with native.
picks.wasm_precedent: bashi/minimp3-wasm (listed among the README's bindings) builds with 'clang --target=wasm32-unknown-unknown -nostdlib' against stub stdlib.h and string.h headers.
claims_to_verify: PCM checksums on .NET match native with -ffp-contract=off (not run)

picks.name: KISS FFT
picks.what: Small mixed-radix FFT (complex, real and N-dimensional) in float, double, int16 or int32 fixed point. BSD-3-Clause. kissfft.hh is a separate C++ header and is not used.
picks.size: The core is about 830 lines: kiss_fft.c 424, kiss_fft.h 184, _kiss_fft_guts.h 189, kiss_fft_log.h 36. kiss_fftr.c adds 171. kiss_fftnd/ndr are optional.
picks.why_good: FP-heavy complex butterflies with recursion through kf_work, and the FIXED_POINT=16/32 builds run the same algorithm in integer arithmetic. It needs only libm, which Phase 1 provides.
picks.blockers:
Compile with -DNDEBUG. Otherwise kiss_fft_log.h references fprintf(stderr), which pulls in __acrt_iob_func, fwrite and fputc on msvc-msil.
Map KISS_FFT_MALLOC/KISS_FFT_FREE to an arena. kiss_fft_alloc's lenmem==NULL path references them. KISS_FFT_TMP_ALLOC (which is also KISS_FFT_MALLOC) allocates at run time in kf_bfly_generic (radices other than 2/3/4/5) and in kiss_fft_stride when fin==fout. A bump arena therefore grows on every such call, so use 2/3/5-smooth sizes with out-of-place transforms, or an arena with a real free.
Do not define USE_SIMD or KISS_FFT_USE_ALLOCA (the C macro; KISSFFT_USE_ALLOCA is the build option). With an arena and NDEBUG, kiss_fft.c compiles through the MSIL backend, and its IR declares only cos, sin and sqrt besides the allocator (verified).
Compile both sides with -ffp-contract=off for bit-exact comparison.
picks.tests: Upstream test/ compares against FFTW3 and NumPy (host-side infrastructure). Phase 1 compares output checksums or SNR with a native build on fixed input.
picks.wasm_precedent: Not verified: kissfft-wasm (npm, Emscripten), kissfft-js (an Emscripten transpile by Chris Cannam) and webfft's kissWasm backend.
claims_to_verify: the three wasm ports exist
outputs on .NET match native (not run)

picks.name: Richards benchmark (JetStream / Sightglass / llvm-test-suite copies)
picks.what: Martin Richards' OS task-scheduler simulation: task control blocks in linked lists, with work dispatched through function pointers. The JetStream repository is BSD-2-Clause (Apple). richards.c has no license header of its own and credits M. J. Jordan and M. Richards.
picks.size: The JetStream richards.c is 375 lines, the Sightglass copy 390 and the llvm-test-suite copy 408.
picks.why_good: Struct- and pointer-heavy code with indirect calls through stored function pointers, an early check of ldftn/calli, with deterministic qpkt_count and hold_count results. Three separate wasm benchmark suites ship it.
picks.blockers:
JetStream copy: remove '#include <emscripten.h>'. There are no keep-alive annotations to remove, because the setup/scheduleIter/getQpktcount/getHoldcount exports come from emcc flags in build.sh. It also includes stdio.h and stdlib.h, but the only call is malloc (createtask line 91, pkt line 108, never freed), so supply a static bump-arena malloc. Add a main that runs the iterations and prints the two counters with puts.
The Sightglass copy also needs bench_start/bench_end stubs and uses unistd/fcntl. The llvm-test-suite copy uses printf throughout, so it needs Phase 3 as written.
picks.tests: Deterministic counters compared with native. The llvm-test-suite copy has .reference_output files; the Sightglass copy has no expected-output files.
picks.wasm_precedent: JetStream 2/3 richards-wasm (built with emcc); Sightglass benchmarks/richards; the llvm-test-suite Misc copy is part of the SingleSource/Benchmarks set that WarpDiff compiled to wasm.
claims_to_verify: the counters on .NET match native (not run)

picks.name: stb_sprintf
picks.what: Printf-family formatter (stbsp_sprintf, stbsp_snprintf, stbsp_vsprintfcb) in pure C, with its own floating-point formatting. MIT or public domain (Unlicense).
picks.size: stb_sprintf.h, 1,906 lines.
picks.why_good: The ideal first varargs test for Phase 3: variadic definitions plus va_list/va_arg over ints, long longs, doubles, pointers and strings, with no libc dependency and output that diffs byte-for-byte against native. STB_SPRINTF_NOFLOAT gives an integer-only first step.
picks.blockers:
The API is made of variadic definitions, and the va_list entry points need va_start in a variadic caller. Verified: compiling through the MSIL backend fails at stb_sprintf.h:1376 with 'variadic function definitions are not supported for MSIL yet'.
Nothing else is missing. The only #includes are stdarg.h and stddef.h, it formats floating point itself (stbsp__real_to_str with its own power-of-ten tables), and the linux-msil IR has no libc declarations. Use STB_SPRINTF_NOUNALIGNED at first to avoid unaligned word loads.
picks.tests: No upstream suite. Diff a table of format strings and values against a native build, and against the host printf for the common subset.
picks.wasm_precedent: stb headers are common in Emscripten builds; raylib's web builds reportedly bundle stb_image and stb_truetype (not verified). No verified wasm user of stb_sprintf specifically.
claims_to_verify: raylib's web builds bundle stb headers

picks.name: zlib (Z_SOLO core)
picks.what: The deflate/inflate compression library (latest release v1.3.2, 2026-02-17). zlib license.
picks.size: The v1.3.2 core .c files total 7,703 lines: adler32 164, compress 99, crc32 983, deflate 2,185, infback 581, inffast 321, inflate 1,413, inftrees 424, trees 1,119, uncompr 101, zutil 313. The headers add more; crc32.h alone is about 9.4k lines of tables. The gz*.c file layer adds 2,000.
picks.why_good: Probably the most-ported C library in wasm, and integer-heavy (bit I/O, hashing, Huffman trees, CRC tables). Compressed output is byte-identical to native for a given level and strategy.
picks.blockers:
Build with -DZ_SOLO. It removes zcalloc/zcfree (declared in zutil.h and defined in zutil.c under !Z_SOLO) and the gz* API in zlib.h. Under Z_SOLO, deflateInit2_ and inflateInit2_ return Z_STREAM_ERROR when zalloc/zfree are 0, so the harness must set them to static-arena functions. Z_SOLO also defines NO_MEMCPY and leaves Z_U4/Z_U8 undefined, so crc32.c falls back to the byte-wise CRC. Leave out gz*.c.
Unity TU: in v1.3.2 the fixed tables moved into inftrees.c (inflate_fixed), so infback.c can follow inflate.c. The only conflict left is PULLBYTE, which the two files define differently: it gives one -Wmacro-redefined warning, and the later definition is the one infback needs. In v1.3.1 and earlier, inflate.c and infback.c both define 'local void fixedtables()', so leave infback.c out there.
Keep DYNAMIC_CRC_TABLE and BUILDFIXED off. Both use z_once (zutil.h), which uses <stdatomic.h> under C11.
crc32.c's inline asm requires __aarch64__, so it is inactive on the MSIL triples. test/example.c and minigzip.c use stdio/printf.
picks.tests: test/example.c round-trip checks (port to puts). Byte-exact compressed output and crc32/adler32 compared with native. Emscripten's test_zlib_benchmark prints sizes and checksums.
picks.wasm_precedent: JetStream 3 (released 2026-03) zlib-wasm, built with 'emcc -s USE_ZLIB=1' around a zpipe.c driver that uses stdio through the Emscripten FS; the Emscripten port -sUSE_ZLIB. Reported but not verified: ffmpeg.wasm and WordPress Playground php-wasm build it; Emscripten test_zzz_zlib; Pyodide libzlib.

picks.what: Burrows-Wheeler block-sorting compressor library. bzip2 (BSD-style) license.

A scan of the 7 files found 33 distinct file-scope statics and no macro defined twice, so they should #include into one TU cleanly (not compiled).

picks.name: Zstandard single-file decoder (zstddeclib.c)
picks.what: The zstd decompressor amalgamated into one C file by the project's own script (create_single_file_decoder.sh). License: BSD-3-Clause or GPL-2.0.
picks.size: The generated zstddeclib.c is about 22,271 lines (29 files inlined, zstd.h included) at v1.5.7, and about 22,517 lines (30 files) at dev.
picks.why_good: A modern codec that browsers run through wasm, already published as a single TU, covering 64-bit bit-stream reading, FSE/Huffman tables and wildcopy loops. Frames carry an XXH64 content checksum, so every decode verifies itself.
picks.blockers:
zstddeclib-in.c already defines ZSTD_DISABLE_ASM 1, DEBUGLEVEL 0 and ZSTD_LEGACY_SUPPORT 0. Add three more defines:
- -DDYNAMIC_BMI2=0 removes the BMI2 target-attribute functions and ZSTD_cpuSupportsBmi2(), the only caller of ZSTD_cpuid's asm/__cpuid.
- -DZSTD_NO_INTRINSICS removes the SSE2 ZSTD_copy16.
- -DNO_PREFETCH removes __builtin_prefetch (or _mm_prefetch on msvc-msil).
On x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-msil clang defines __GNUC__, so three groups of __asm__(".p2align N") and __asm__("nop") loop-alignment hacks in zstd_decompress_block.c, guarded only by __GNUC__ && __x86_64__, stay in. Patch them out, because MSIL rejects inline asm. On x86_64-pc-windows-msvc-msil __GNUC__ is not predefined, so they are already off.
Allocation: zstddeclib-in.c defines ZSTD_DEPS_NEED_MALLOC, which maps ZSTD_malloc/calloc/free to malloc/calloc/free. Define arena versions in the harness, or replace zstd_deps.h, which is documented as replaceable for no-libc builds.
Decode with ZSTD_initStaticDCtx (in the ZSTD_STATIC_LINKING_ONLY section) on a static, 8-aligned workspace sized by ZSTD_estimateDCtxSize(); it does not allocate. Without __GNUC__ (the msvc triple), ZSTD_memcpy/memmove/memset expand to the libc names, which clang turns into intrinsics.
picks.tests: build_decoder_test.sh decodes testcard-zstd.inl and compares; tests/golden-decompression; XXH64 frame checksums.
picks.wasm_precedent: zstddec (npm, donmccurdy) runs create_single_file_decoder.sh and then 'emcc zstddeclib.c ... -o zstddec.wasm'. Reported but not verified: the single_file_libs README's figure of about 26 kB added to an Emscripten project, and @hpcc-js/wasm-zstd (v1.5.7 via emsdk).
claims_to_verify: with these flags (and the asm patch on linux-msil) zstddeclib.c compiles through the MSIL backend on both triples (not compiled)

picks.name: Brotli decoder (c/common + c/dec)
picks.what: Google's compression format (HTTP content-encoding, WOFF2), using the decoder half of the C library. MIT. c/ is C; the repo also holds Java, Go, C# and JS ports.
picks.size: About 8.8k lines of decoder code on master: c/common .c 1,064, c/dec .c 3,745 (decode.c 3,023), internal headers about 3,050, public decode headers about 900. The 122,784-byte static dictionary is embedded as c/common/dictionary_inc.h (5,847 lines, 470 KB of text).
picks.why_good: Its 122 KB constant dictionary and transform tables stress the data image (the RVA blob and .cctor copy) far more than typical programs do. Behind them is a real decoder state machine with golden decode tests.
picks.blockers:
Allocation: when both callbacks are NULL, BrotliDecoderCreateInstance calls malloc and free directly rather than through BrotliDefaultAllocFunc, and shared_dictionary.c also calls malloc directly. Define malloc/free in the harness. Passing static-arena brotli_alloc_func/brotli_free_func avoids the calls at run time but not the references.
SIMD and asm are not an issue on x86_64. The decoder's only SIMD is NEON, and platform.h's only inline asm is the ARM rbit and the aarch64 prfm prefetch. Prefetch becomes __builtin_prefetch, or _mm_prefetch with <intrin.h> on msvc-msil.
A scan of the 12 .c files in c/common and c/dec (master and v1.2.0) found 87 file-scope statics, all distinct, and no conflicting macros. They should #include into one TU; BROTLI_STATIC_INIT defaults to NONE.
picks.tests: tests/testdata *.compressed files with their originals (golden decodes); round-trip scripts.

picks.name: MD4C (Markdown parser)
picks.what: Fast CommonMark/GFM Markdown parser with SAX-like callbacks, plus an optional HTML renderer. MIT.
picks.size: About 10.8k lines in 6 src files: md4c.c 7,386, md4c.h 495, md4c-html.c 658, md4c-html.h 68, entity.c 2,186, entity.h 43.
picks.why_good: A real parser with pointer-heavy line and span processing, mark stacks and output through function-pointer callbacks. About 650 CommonMark spec examples give it an unusually large deterministic test corpus.
picks.blockers:
Parser (md4c.c): it calls malloc/realloc/free directly (about 17/16/23 sites; MD_PARSER has no allocator hook). It also calls qsort (l.1874), bsearch (l.1945), strchr, memchr and memcmp. Define all of them in C in the harness. qsort and bsearch take callbacks, so importing them would need native-to-managed callbacks (Phase 3), and C has no spelling for the explicit import attribute yet.
The 4 sprintf calls (l.7314-7326) sit inside '#if 0' and never compile. Leave DEBUG undefined, because it enables MD_ASSERT (fprintf and exit).
HTML renderer: md4c-html.c has 4 snprintf calls (l.279, 396, 406, 419), debug_log_callback calls fprintf(stderr) (l.614), and entity.c uses bsearch with a strncmp comparator. The shipped renderer is therefore Phase 3. For Phase 1, patch those 5 calls (for example with an itoa) or write a small renderer in the harness.
On the msvc triple, defining CRT names such as malloc, qsort and strchr in the TU may draw -Winconsistent-dllimport where the UCRT declares them _ACRTIMP. This is not tested; memset and memcmp were fine for BLAKE2.
picks.tests: test/*.txt holds the CommonMark spec and extension examples with expected HTML. Upstream runs them with run-testsuite.py against md2html, which uses stdio. Embed the examples as data for Phase 1.
picks.wasm_precedent: markdown-wasm (rsms; its README says it is built on md4c). md4w (Zig/C to wasm, used by esm.sh; not verified).
claims_to_verify: harness definitions of malloc, qsort, strchr and the like are accepted on msvc-msil when the UCRT headers are visible
md4w is based on md4c and used by esm.sh

picks.name: Expat (XML parser)
picks.what: Stream-oriented (SAX-style) XML 1.0 parser library. C99, MIT. Latest release 2.9.0 (2026-10-05).
picks.size: 2.9.0 lib/ .c files: xmlparse.c 9,705, xmltok.c 1,596 and xmlrole.c 1,256, plus xmltok_impl.c 1,819 and xmltok_ns.c 125 (both #included by xmltok.c). That is about 14.5k lines before headers.
picks.why_good: A widely embedded parser with a switch-based tokenizer, per-encoding tables of function pointers and a memory suite of function pointers. tests/runtests is a large pass/fail unit suite, and the W3C conformance suite runs through xmlwf.
picks.blockers:
Phase 1 rejects these references even if they never run:
- 10 fprintf(stderr) calls in xmlparse.c (l.851, 1113, 8965, 8985-9012, 9108)
- getenv in getDebugLevel (l.9689, with strtoul and errno)
All but one are under '#if XML_GE == 1' and gated at run time by EXPAT_MALLOC_DEBUG, EXPAT_ACCOUNTING_DEBUG and EXPAT_ENTITY_DEBUG. The ENTROPY_DEBUG fprintf and its getenv("EXPAT_ENTROPY_DEBUG") are compiled unconditionally, so even XML_GE=0 leaves one fprintf and one getenv.
Hash-salt entropy: the sources are chosen by HAVE_ARC4RANDOM_BUF, HAVE_ARC4RANDOM, HAVE_GETENTROPY, HAVE_GETRANDOM, HAVE_SYSCALL_GETRANDOM and XML_DEV_URANDOM, plus rand_s on _WIN32. Unless arc4random is used, the fallback (gettimeofday XOR getpid, or GetSystemTimeAsFileTime/GetCurrentProcessId on _WIN32) is always compiled; XML_POOR_ENTROPY only silences the #error. startParsing references generate_hash_secret_salt even when XML_SetHashSalt was called.
For a hand-built TU, define XML_GE=0 or 1 (xmlparse.c #errors if it is undefined) and pass -DXML_POOR_ENTROPY; XML_DTD requires XML_GE=1. The CMake options are EXPAT_GE and EXPAT_DTD; autoconf hard-codes both to 1. Allocation goes through XML_ParserCreate_MM.
Phase 3's host libc resolves everything. A Phase 1 build needs source patches for the ENTROPY_DEBUG output, getDebugLevel and the time/pid fallback.
picks.tests: tests/runtests (large C unit suite with pass/fail); xmlwf plus xmltest.sh for the W3C XML test suite.

picks.name: tree-sitter runtime + one generated grammar
picks.what: Incremental GLR parsing runtime; lib/src/lib.c #includes all 13 runtime .c files. Each grammar is a generated parser.c (tables and a lexer switch) with an optional scanner.c. The runtime is C (the CLI and tests are Rust), MIT; latest release v0.27.1 (2026-10-08).
picks.size: The runtime is about 20k lines in 34 files (estimate, not measured). Grammar parser.c sizes on master: json 1,062 lines (no external scanner), html 2,300, css 17,861, go 61,521, javascript 94,268, c 118,872, python 130,003, rust 205,906, bash 350,631, ruby 471,247.
picks.why_good: Generated grammars are the best available stress test for huge switch statements (ts_lex) and very large static uint16 tables in the data image, and the GLR runtime is pointer-heavy (ref-counted subtrees, stack versions). A grammar's parser.c alone also makes a large compile-only stress test from Phase 1.
picks.blockers:
Several runtime files reference Phase 3 features, and no macro removes them:
- lexer.c defines the variadic ts_lexer__log (TSLexer.log, va_start + vsnprintf).
- alloc.c's default allocators call fprintf(stderr) and abort(), and stay referenced through the ts_current_* initializers even after ts_set_allocator.
- parser.c's LOG macros use snprintf, and its dot-graph code uses fprintf/fputs/fdopen.
- stack.c and tree.c have dot-graph printers (fprintf, plus dup/fdopen in tree.c).
- subtree.c's ts_subtree_string, which ts_node_string calls, uses snprintf.
A Phase 1 build is possible only with source patches to those files, plus:
- atomic.h patched to its __TINYC__ plain path. Otherwise clang uses __atomic builtins on linux-msil, and on msvc-msil _WIN32 pulls in <windows.h> and InterlockedIncrement/Decrement.
- -DNDEBUG.
- Harness definitions of malloc/calloc/realloc/free and of iswspace and iswalnum, which query.c calls.
wasm_store.c compiles to inert stubs without TREE_SITTER_FEATURE_WASM.
Grammars: tree_sitter/alloc.h maps ts_malloc and friends to malloc and the others unless TREE_SITTER_REUSE_ALLOCATOR is defined. External scanners call more of libc. javascript and css use only isw* functions; python uses calloc/free/memcpy/assert; bash, html and ruby add strcmp, strlen, strncpy, strchr, towupper and others. Start with tree-sitter-json, which has no scanner.
picks.tests: Grammar repositories carry test/corpus/*.txt files that pair source text with the expected S-expression tree. Without ts_node_string, walk the tree with TSTreeCursor and print node types through puts.
picks.wasm_precedent: web-tree-sitter (npm) built with Emscripten; grammars compile to .wasm with 'tree-sitter build --wasm'; lib/src/wasm-stdlib provides a tiny libc for wasm scanners.

picks.name: wasm3 (WebAssembly interpreter)
picks.what: Fast WebAssembly interpreter (the M3 'meta machine': each operation is a function that calls the next), with optional WASI support. MIT. The project was revived in 2026: v0.9.0 and v0.9.1-beta.1 came out on 2026-09-10.
picks.size: main: source/ has 49 .c/.h files and 36,367 lines, about 30.0k of them outside the m3_api_* bindings (libc/WASI/uvwasi/tracer). v0.5.0 had 37 files and 13,597 lines (about 10.5k core).
picks.why_good: Running WebAssembly inside .NET through this compiler is the most on-theme test there is. Every interpreted op is an indirect call through a function pointer with 5-6 arguments, the worst case for calli and per-call frame cost, and it can run embedded .wasm modules such as coremark.wasm against native wasm3.
picks.blockers:
Both v0.5.0 and main define the variadic m3_CallV and m3_GetResultsV, plus m3_CallVL/m3_GetResultsVL, which take a va_list. With d_m3VerboseErrorMessages=1 (the default) they also define a variadic m3Error that calls vsnprintf. Unpatched, it therefore needs Phase 3.
A Phase 1 build needs those functions patched out, plus:
- -Dd_m3VerboseErrorMessages=0.
- -DM3_HAS_TAIL_CALL=0. On x86_64, main uses __attribute__((musttail)), which MSIL LowerCall rejects; this define also drops preserve_none.
- -Dd_m3MaxNativeStack=0. The default uses __builtin_frame_address(0), which Phase 1 diagnoses, and a static M3_THREAD_LOCAL in m3_core.c.
- -Dd_m3HasPosixHost=0 -Dd_m3HasWin32Host=0, to get m3_host_none.h instead of mmap/sigaction/sigsetjmp/pthread_getattr_np or VirtualAlloc.
- d_m3FixedHeap with harness malloc/calloc/realloc/free.
- Logging and tracing off.
- A harness abort() for m3_Abort.
libm is fine. The core calls ceil, floor, trunc, sqrt and rint and their f variants, all Phase 1 imports for ucrtbase and libm.so.6. fabs and copysign lower inline, and it never calls fmin, fmax or nearbyint.
Without tail calls, each op adds a .NET frame until a loop, trap or return unwinds the chain. This is an inference: docs/Interpreter.md only says that loops, traps and returns unwind the stack. Measure stack depth on long straight-line blocks and on deep wasm recursion.
The WASI host (m3_api_wasi.c) and the CLI need stdio (Phase 3).
picks.tests: The WebAssembly spec suite through test/run-spec-test.py, which drives the wasm3 CLI (stdio and WASI, so Phase 3). With the Phase 1 patches, run embedded modules and check exported-function results.
picks.wasm_precedent: Not verified: wasm3 is itself compiled to wasm and can run itself, and webassembly.sh runs it in the browser.
claims_to_verify: the .NET stack depth reached without tail calls on realistic modules
a patched build compiles through the MSIL backend (not tried)
wasm3 self-hosting and webassembly.sh

picks.name: Lua 5.4 (onelua.c single-TU build)
picks.what: The reference Lua interpreter and VM. MIT.
picks.size: 5.4.9's .c/.h files total 29,450 lines (excluding ltests and onelua.c). onelua.c, in the repo root, #includes the whole interpreter into one TU: MAKE_LUA by default, or MAKE_LIB for the library only. Current releases are 5.5.1 (2026-07-24) and 5.4.9 (2026-08-10).
picks.why_good: A real VM in one TU, with switch or computed-goto dispatch, setjmp-based errors, a GC over pointer-heavy object graphs and a deeply recursive parser. The official test suite is assertion-based and self-checking.
picks.blockers:
Built as C, errors use setjmp/longjmp (ldo.c l.53-73; _setjmp/_longjmp with LUA_USE_POSIX), which is Phase 3. LUAI_THROW/LUAI_TRY can be predefined, but redefining LUAI_THROW to abort does not get the core below Phase 3: lua_pushfstring/luaO_pushfstring and luaL_error are variadic definitions, and lua_number2str uses snprintf (luaconf.h l.420/597).
Other libc use:
- strtod and localeconv
- fwrite through lua_writestring
- stdio in lauxlib/liolib
- time/clock in loslib
- dlopen in loadlib.c (use the fallback)
- signal() in lua.c
onelua.c itself includes setjmp.h, signal.h, locale.h and time.h. The allocator is pluggable (lua_Alloc).
Computed goto: lvm.c enables LUA_USE_JUMPTABLE under __GNUC__. A constant label table plus indirectbr compiles on both triples at -O0 and -O2 (blockaddress-errors.ll). Only computed goto through selects/phis has actually been run, not a table stored in data. x86_64-pc-windows-msvc-msil does not predefine __GNUC__, so Lua uses switch dispatch there.
picks.tests: Official testes/ (all.lua, api.lua, strings.lua, coroutine.lua, gc.lua, ...); some parts need the ltests.c C-API library.
picks.wasm_precedent: wasmoon (npm, Lua 5.4): its build.sh runs emcc over the official lua/lua sources except lua.c and luac.c. Emscripten's test_benchmark.py builds lua as C. emscripten-forge lua (not verified).

picks.name: Box2D v3 (C library and unit tests)
picks.what: 2D rigid-body physics engine, rewritten in C for v3. MIT. The library, tests, shared and benchmark code are C; the samples app is mostly C++ (imgui).
picks.size: main: src 38,622 + include 5,726 lines (44.3k), plus test 10,151 and shared 2,867 (57.4k in all); 43 library TUs. v3.1.1 (latest release, 2025-06-04): 34.1k lines for src+include, 37.2k with tests; 35 TUs.
picks.why_good: FP-heavy simulation with a built-in cross-platform determinism hash, the strongest FP-equivalence check on the list (it catches contraction, conversion and ordering differences). Its trig functions are its own approximations rather than libm.
picks.blockers:
Atomics: v3.1.1 has src/atomic.h (b2AtomicInt/U32). On main, the b2AtomicInt/U32/I64 types are in core.h and the functions in platform.h. _MSC_VER, which msvc-msil predefines, selects _Interlocked*, except that main's b2AtomicLoadInt uses __atomic_load_n under clang. Atomics are Phase 3, or patch them to plain loads and stores for single-threaded use.
b2Pause() is __asm__ __volatile__("pause") under (__GNUC__ || __clang__) on x86 (solver.c at v3.1.1, platform.h on main). It is called in solver spin-waits whatever the worker count. Both MSIL triples select it and inline asm is rejected, so patch it to an empty body.
Other settings:
- Set BOX2D_DISABLE_SIMD (default OFF; on main it also forces BOX2D_AVX2 off), because the x86_64 predefines would select SSE2/AVX2.
- Use workerCount=1 or no task system.
- Use b2SetAllocator, because the default allocators reference malloc.
sqrtf is a Phase 1 import. The 35-43 TUs need Phase 2, or a unity build (static-name collisions not checked). The tests use printf.
picks.tests: test/ unit tests (collision, distance, dynamic tree, world) and test_determinism.c. v3.1.1 expects hash 0x35467e1e at sleep step 288. main expects 0x36564C94 at step 295 (0x29D0B92D at step 256 with BOX2D_DOUBLE_PRECISION) and also runs built-in-scheduler and SSE2-fallback variants.
picks.wasm_precedent: Upstream build_emscripten.sh (present on main and at v3.1.1) builds the unit tests with Emscripten. box2d3-wasm reportedly powers browser games (not verified).
claims_to_verify: a unity build of the library compiles without static-name collisions

picks.name: jq
picks.what: Command-line JSON processor with a bytecode compiler and VM for its filter language. Latest release jq-1.8.2 (2026-06-20). License: MIT, plus the ICU license for decNumber and David M. Gay's dtoa/g_fmt notices; the docs are CC BY 3.0.
picks.size: About 28k lines in 44 src/*.c/.h files (estimate, not measured), plus vendored decNumber and an optional Oniguruma submodule.
picks.why_good: tests/jq.test holds 550 deterministic program/input/expected-output cases at jq-1.8.2 (596 on master), a strong golden-output corpus. It covers a recursive compiler over ASTs, a backtracking VM, ref-counted values, its own dtoa and heavy FP formatting.
picks.blockers:
Needs malloc, stdio and printf, plus variadic definitions (jv_string_fmt and the error helpers).
Thread-local state goes mainly through pthread keys, with __thread as the fallback:
- On Linux, jv.c uses pthread_key_create/pthread_getspecific/pthread_once for the decNumber context and pthread_once for the hash seed. The __thread at jv.c l.258 is only in Heimdal's Windows emulation.
- jv_alloc.c uses pthread_key and pthread_once, and falls back to __thread (or __declspec(thread)) only when those or atexit are missing.
- jv_dtoa_tsd.c keeps the dtoa context in a pthread key.
Replacing TLS with statics therefore also means stubbing pthread_key_* and pthread_once. There is no setjmp; longjmp appears only in comments.
It is multi-file with a bison/flex parser generated on the host, so it also needs Phase 2. Use --without-oniguruma (or --with-oniguruma=builtin) and optionally --disable-decnum.

picks.name: libsodium (with its test/default golden suite)
picks.what: Portable cryptography library implementing the NaCl API (secretbox, box, sign, AEADs, Argon2, BLAKE2 and more). ISC.
picks.size: src/libsodium has 143 .c files on stable (145 on master) plus 6 .S files, about 59k lines (estimate, not measured). test/default has 101 programs with 101 .exp files on stable (104 on master).
picks.why_good: A long-running cross-runtime wasm benchmark whose every test output is byte-compared to a golden .exp file. It is integer-heavy constant-time crypto across about 145 TUs, which also makes it a good Phase 2 linker workload.
picks.blockers:
The test harness (test/default/cmptest.h) uses printf, fprintf, fopen, perror and fflush (Phase 3). randombytes needs a deterministic implementation via randombytes_set_implementation.
Configure with --disable-asm and no -march flags. HAVE_CPUID, HAVE_AMD64_ASM and HAVE_AVX_ASM are then undefined, so on linux-msil _cpuid zero-fills and CPU detection compiles out.
On msvc-msil, however, runtime.c l.153 calls __cpuid whenever _MSC_VER and _M_X64 are defined, regardless of HAVE_CPUID, and this fork's clang diagnoses __cpuid on MSIL. Patch that call, or use the linux triple.
The SSE/AVX intrinsic implementations are enabled by separate checks (HAVE_EMMINTRIN_H, HAVE_TMMINTRIN_H, HAVE_SMMINTRIN_H, HAVE_AVX2INTRIN_H) that --disable-asm does not touch. Leave them undefined by hand.
sodium_init's lock uses CRITICAL_SECTION plus InterlockedCompareExchange on _WIN32, a pthread mutex with HAVE_PTHREAD, __sync with HAVE_ATOMIC_OPS, and is otherwise a no-op, so linux-msil without those macros needs no atomics. Avoid sodium_malloc (mmap/mprotect). About 145 TUs (Phase 2).
picks.tests: Each test/default/*.c output is compared byte-for-byte with its .exp file. BENCHMARKS mode times the primitives.

picks.name: musl libm (src/math)
picks.what: musl's portable C math library (fdlibm/FreeBSD-derived, plus Arm optimized-routines exp/log/pow). MIT.
picks.size: At v1.2.6 the top level of src/math has 232 .c and 10 .h files, 17,883 lines (counted on wasi-libc's subtree copy, which differs in 11 files). It can be used piecemeal.
picks.why_good: Every wasi-sdk C program runs this code, and its dense bit-level FP (union punning, FORCE_EVAL volatile tricks, double-double evaluation, exact rounding) finds FP codegen bugs that simple programs miss. long double is IEEE double on both MSIL triples, so musl's LDBL_MANT_DIG==DBL_MANT_DIG paths simply forward to the double functions.
picks.blockers:
Use only the generic top-level src/math/*.c files; the arch subdirectories contain asm and inline asm.
fenv calls: fmaf.c and fmal.c call feraiseexcept, fetestexcept, feclearexcept and fegetround, and fmal.c also calls fesetround. nearbyint.c, nearbyintf.c, nearbyintl.c, lrint.c, lrintl.c and llrintl.c call fetestexcept and feclearexcept. Stub these in the harness or skip those files. Everything else raises exceptions only through FORCE_EVAL arithmetic.
It needs musl's internal headers (libm.h and the arch float_eval/endian bits).
Name clashes with the Phase 1 math imports are not a problem. A TU definition wins for direct calls and for SelectionDAG libcalls of the same name, and P/Invokes are emitted only for undefined functions; a definition with a different type is an error. Rename (for example -Dsin=musl_sin) only to call musl's and the host's versions side by side.
Compare bit-exactly against musl built natively, not against UCRT or glibc, which can differ in the last ulp.

picks.name: SQLite (amalgamation)
picks.what: Embedded SQL database engine, shipped as the single-file sqlite3.c amalgamation. Public domain.
picks.size: 3.54.0: sqlite3.c 271,072 lines, shell.c 39,899, sqlite3.h 14,447, sqlite3ext.h 745. One TU by design.
picks.why_good: The biggest real-world single TU, with a huge VDBE dispatch switch, function-pointer VFS and method tables, 64-bit integer and FP formatting and its own printf engine over va_list. Its wasm use is enormous, and SQL scripts give deterministic output to diff against native.
picks.blockers:
Variadic definitions are core to the engine. The printf engine is sqlite3_str_vappendf; there are 44 va_start sites and no SQLITE_OMIT option for them, and the old name sqlite3VXPrintf no longer appears. Even setting up the heap calls the variadic sqlite3_config. So SQLite needs Phase 3 whatever the configuration.
The rest configures away:
- SQLITE_THREADSAFE=0 sets SQLITE_MAX_WORKER_THREADS to 0, which removes pthread_create, and defines SQLITE_MUTEX_OMIT.
- SQLITE_OMIT_LOAD_EXTENSION.
- SQLITE_OS_OTHER=1 with an application-supplied VFS, sqlite3_os_init and sqlite3_os_end (or memdb / :memory:).
- SQLITE_ZERO_MALLOC + SQLITE_ENABLE_MEMSYS5 + sqlite3_config(SQLITE_CONFIG_HEAP) for a malloc-free static heap.
- SQLITE_OMIT_WAL, and leave SQLITE_USE_ALLOCA unset.
The amalgamation contains no 'long double', so MSIL's double-only long double does not matter. It still needs libc string functions and localtime (host libc, Phase 3). shell.c needs stdio and signals.

Varargs everywhere (PyErr_Format, Py_BuildValue, PyArg_Parse*). Atomics are mandatory: 3.14's Include/cpython/pyatomic.h uses GCC builtins, C11 stdatomic or MSVC intrinsics, and otherwise #errors with 'no available pyatomic implementation'. Thread-local state uses _Py_thread_local (pyport.h; for example pystate.c's _Py_tss_tstate). All of these are Phase 3.
Stack-overflow protection: _Py_get_machine_stack_pointer() uses __builtin_frame_address(0), which Phase 1 diagnoses, and compares it with limits taken from pthread_getattr_np or GetCurrentThreadStackLimits. MSIL's frame model (IL locals plus localloc) needs a deliberate mapping for this.
Configure flags: --without-computed-gotos (or let computed gotos compile through IndirectBrExpand), --without-mimalloc (it defaults on when stdatomic.h exists) and --with-build-python (required when cross-compiling).
Without dlopen, modules must be static via Modules/Setup.local, and the stdlib must be frozen, zipped or on the host filesystem. Exclude _ctypes/libffi. Hundreds of TUs, so the Phase 2 linker must work at scale.
picks.tests: regrtest ('python -m test', about 500 test modules); the WASI Tier 2 builder's subset is a good first target.
picks.wasm_precedent: PEP 11 lists wasm32-unknown-wasip1 as Tier 2 (WASI SDK, Wasmtime) and wasm32-unknown-emscripten as Tier 3. Also Pyodide and the Tools/wasm build scripts. The 3.14 docs (the WebAssembly platforms section of Doc/library/intro.rst) list the limits: no process APIs, a limited socket module, threading and signal modules unavailable or not working, restricted file I/O.
claims_to_verify: about 500 regrtest modules
the C line count

picks.name: PostgreSQL in single-user mode (as PGlite does it)
picks.what: A full relational database server. PGlite builds Postgres to wasm and runs it in single-user mode as a library. PostgreSQL License; PGlite is dual Apache-2.0/PostgreSQL. Postgres is C apart from the optional LLVM JIT (four .cpp files, built only with --with-llvm), which is excluded.
picks.size: About 950k lines of C plus 121k lines of SQL tests (Debian postgresql-17 counts, not re-measured).
picks.why_good: The flagship example of 'people now run X in wasm', using sigsetjmp-based error handling (PG_TRY/ereport) at scale, with pg_regress as a huge deterministic golden-SQL corpus.
picks.blockers:
ereport ERROR unwinds through sigsetjmp/siglongjmp (PG_TRY in elog.h:391, elog.c:2013): Phase 3.
The postmaster forks a backend per connection, so use single-user mode (postgres --single) as PGlite does. Replace SysV/POSIX shared memory and semaphores with process-local memory.
PG18 removed --disable-spinlocks and --disable-atomics and now requires 32-bit atomics, so supply atomics (Phase 3) and patch s_lock.h/port/atomics wherever they pick native x86_64 inline asm or MSVC intrinsics. PG17 still has both configure options.
The data directory and WAL need a host or in-memory filesystem. Extensions are loaded with dlopen, so link them statically. The build needs bison, flex and perl, and the code uses variadic elog/errmsg.
picks.tests: pg_regress: the REL_18_STABLE src/test/regress parallel_schedule lists 231 tests with expected/*.out. Also isolation tests and Perl TAP tests.
picks.wasm_precedent: PGlite (ElectricSQL, Emscripten): its README says it runs Postgres in single-user mode with no fork, one user and connection. Extensions such as pgvector are supported. The figures of about 3 MB gzipped and about 16k stars were not re-checked.
claims_to_verify: the Debian line counts
which spinlock and atomics paths s_lock.h and port/atomics select on each MSIL triple

picks.name: GCC C torture tests (gcc.c-torture/execute)
picks.what: GCC's execution torture tests: self-checking C programs (mostly GNU C) that call abort() on failure. The LLVM WebAssembly backend was brought up on them. Covered by GCC's GPL-3.0-or-later; the test files themselves mostly have no header.
picks.size: 1,699 top-level execute/*.c files, plus ieee/ (78 .c) and builtins/ (59 tests, each a test file plus a -lib.c helper).
picks.why_good: The densest compiler-bug finder available: about 1,700 self-checking corner-case programs (integer promotion, bitfields, struct passing, switch lowering, overflow, FP edge cases), each run at every optimization level. About 74% of the top-level tests (about 1,255) need nothing beyond abort/exit, the mem* intrinsics and a few libm calls (floor, fabs, pow, copysign).
picks.blockers:
abort: force-include a header with 'static void abort(void) { __builtin_trap(); }'. This compiles cleanly on msvc-msil against the tests' 'extern void abort (void);' declarations. '#define abort() __builtin_trap()' fails with 'too many arguments provided to function-like macro invocation'.
exit also needs a harness definition. C has no spelling for the explicit import attribute yet: clang's import_module/import_name are WebAssembly-only and are ignored with a warning, and nothing in clang emits msil-import-module. Clang treats exit as noreturn, so a definition that returns is undefined behaviour. Have it print a status marker with puts and then trap, and let the runner key on the marker.
Skip or defer, by count over the 1,699 top-level files:
- varargs 84 (Phase 3)
- inline asm 79 (mostly empty asm("") barriers, which MSIL rejects)
- label addresses/goto* 44 (plain computed goto works through IndirectBrExpand; BlockAddress outside an indirectbr is diagnosed)
- vector_size 42 (Phase 4 SIMD)
- long double 36 (only where it must be wider than double, which it is not on MSIL)
- nested functions about 25 (clang rejects them)
- _Complex 22 (multiply/divide need __mulsc3/__divdc3, Phase 3)
- alloca/VLAs 14 (Phase 3)
- __int128 14 (division needs __divti3, Phase 3)
- setjmp 6 (Phase 3)
- __builtin_return_address/frame_address 5
Tests that call strlen (31), strcmp (30), memcmp (27), malloc (24), printf (24), strcpy (18), sprintf (12), abs (6) or ffs (6) need Phase 3 or harness definitions. builtins/ tests are two TUs, so they need Phase 2 or a one-TU wrapper.
picks.tests: Self-checking: exit 0 (or the harness's exit-0 marker) means pass, and abort means fail. Run each test at -O0/-O1/-O2/-Os. llvm-test-suite already carries a copy with CMake skip lists at SingleSource/Regression/C/gcc-c-torture/execute.
picks.wasm_precedent: Strong. On release/8.x, the LLVM WebAssembly backend README says bring-up used the GCC torture suite because it does not need C library support. That is not literally true: the tests call abort/exit, some call printf/malloc/string.h, and the waterfall linked musl. known_gcc_test_failures.txt lists 57 C failures grouped as computed gotos, __builtin_return_address, an asm constraint, __builtin_setjmp, and nested functions that clang does not support. WebKit imported the tests for wasm (bug 170740; not verified).
claims_to_verify: force-included static abort/exit definitions compile against tests that #include <stdlib.h> on the msvc triple, where the UCRT declares them _ACRTIMP
WebKit bug 170740
the ~1,255 clean-test figure holds on an actual MSIL run (it comes from a grep)

picks.name: c-testsuite
picks.what: Conformance suite for small C compilers: 220 single-file tests (tests/single-exec/00001.c to 00220.c), each with a .c.expected output file and a .c.tags file. The harness is MIT; the tests carry origin notes only (150 from scc, 69 from tinycc, one with none).
picks.size: 220 .c files (219 also have .c.otags), from a few lines up to a few hundred each.
picks.why_good: A simple pass rule (exit 0 and byte-equal output) and libc-free majority make it an early conformance check of basic-to-intermediate language features that small compilers often get wrong.
picks.blockers:
Tags in use: portable (all 220), c89 174, needs-cpp 98, needs-libc 63, c99 43, c11 2.
needs-cpp means the test relies on the preprocessor, not on C++, so do not exclude it.
needs-libc does not reliably mark libc use. 8 tests without it declare libc functions themselves and call them: 00025 (strlen) and 00210, 00211, 00213, 00214, 00215, 00217 and 00218 (printf). So 157 tests lack needs-libc, and 149 of those truly need no libc and run in Phase 1. Their expected output is empty; they report through the exit status.
The rest need printf and friends (Phase 3); for example, 00200.c prints with '%s %d %d'. Classify tests by grepping their calls, not by their tags.
picks.tests: Pass means exit code 0 and stdout+stderr byte-equal to the .c.expected file, within a 5-minute timeout.
picks.wasm_precedent: Weak. No wasm-specific runner was found; the ppci compiler (which has a wasm backend) documents running it (not verified).
claims_to_verify: ppci runs it
per-test licenses, which must be traced upstream to scc and tinycc

picks.name: Csmith (differential random testing)
picks.what: Generator of random C programs free of undefined behavior. Each program prints a checksum of its global state, for differential compiler testing. BSD-2-Clause. The generator is C++, but it runs only on the host; the generated programs and runtime headers are C.
picks.size: Unlimited. Each generated program is one .c file of a few hundred to a few thousand lines, plus the runtime headers (csmith.h or csmith_minimal.h, and a platform header).
picks.why_good: An unlimited stream of UB-free programs whose checksum must match native clang. It is the standard way to fuzz a new backend for miscompiles in integer promotion, volatile accesses, deep pointer chains, bitfields and packed structs.
picks.blockers:
Simplest Phase 1 setup: -DCSMITH_MINIMAL -DNO_PRINTF. This uses csmith_minimal.h instead of platform_generic.h and prints the checksum with putchar (my_puts/put_hex), so no custom platform header or printf shim is needed. Its transparent_crc is a plain sum rather than a CRC, so it catches fewer differences.
Run the generator with --no-argc. Otherwise the generated main calls strcmp(argv[1], "1"); csmith_minimal.h declares strcmp extern unless -DTCC, which supplies a local definition.
With the full runtime instead: NOT_PRINT_CHECKSUM removes the 'checksum = %X' printf, but transparent_crc still references printf behind a runtime flag, so a custom platform header and a printf shim are needed.
Other generator flags: --no-int128/--no-uint128 (avoid __divti3), --no-bitfields, --no-packed-struct, --no-volatiles, --no-volatile-pointers, --no-float, --no-builtins, --no-hash-value-printf, --no-longlong (makes the CRC 32-bit), --no-math64 and --no-safe-math.
safe_math uses only fabs/fabsf, which are intrinsics. csmith.h includes string.h, math.h and float.h without calling anything from them. random_inc.h includes assert.h, so use -DNDEBUG. Some programs loop forever, so run under a timeout.
picks.tests: Differential: the checksum must match native clang/MSVC output for the same program at -O0 and -O2.
picks.wasm_precedent: Not verified: Emscripten's tests/fuzz shipped csmith_driver.py, creduce_tester.py and csmith.h, and LLVM bug 27518 'Fuzz failures on wasm backend' (2016) came from Csmith.
claims_to_verify: a CSMITH_MINIMAL + NO_PRINTF program generated with --no-argc compiles through the MSIL backend with no other libc references
the Emscripten fuzz scripts and LLVM bug 27518

picks.name: Sightglass benchmarks (C subset: 19 shootout kernels plus quicksort and richards; bz2 later)
picks.what: Wasmtime/Cranelift's benchmark suite. Its C programs include 19 shootout kernels (ackermann, base64, ctype, ed25519, fib2, gimli, heapsort, keccak, matrix, memmove, minicsv, nestedloop, random, ratelimit, seqhash, sieve, switch, xblabla20, xchacha20), plus quicksort, richards and bz2. Sightglass is dual Apache-2.0/MIT; shootout/src carries the Benchmarks Game 3-clause BSD license.
picks.size: Each program is one .c file of about 50-800 lines plus sightglass.h. bz2 is a single file of about 170 KB.
picks.why_good: Small, real kernels straight from the wasm runtime world, covering 64-bit crypto (ed25519, keccak, chacha, gimli), recursion (ackermann, fib2), switch dispatch, memory moves, sorting and function pointers (richards).
picks.blockers:
sightglass.h declares bench_start/bench_end with import_module("bench"), which clang ignores on MSIL, leaving them undefined. Replace the header with one that stubs them. bench_read_long uses open/read/close/strtol; replace it with the compiled-in default. BLACK_BOX uses a volatile function pointer. Compile with -DNDEBUG to drop assert.
libc use per program:
- nothing beyond bench_*: gimli, keccak
- memset only: ed25519
- printf only: ackermann, fib2, nestedloop, random, quicksort, sieve (static array)
- calloc/free: heapsort (includes math.h but calls nothing), memmove, xblabla20, xchacha20
- minicsv: strlen, memmove, isspace, abort
- seqhash: calloc/free, abort
- base64: malloc/calloc/free, strchr, printf
- matrix: calloc/free, printf
- ratelimit: malloc/calloc/free, printf
- switch: malloc/free, printf
- ctype: malloc/free, isalnum/isalpha/isdigit/islower/isspace/isupper, tolower/toupper, memset, printf
- richards: malloc
Provide an arena malloc/calloc and the small string/ctype functions in the harness, and turn the final printf lines into puts or a checksum.
bz2 reads its input with open/read and contains fopen/fread/fwrite/fprintf/exit/strcat/strcmp, so in practice it is Phase 3.
picks.tests: The 19 shootout kernels, bz2 and quicksort ship *.stdout.expected and *.stderr.expected. richards has none, and nine shootout stdout files are empty (ed25519, gimli, heapsort, keccak, memmove, minicsv, seqhash, xblabla20, xchacha20), so add a checksum and compare with native.
picks.wasm_precedent: Built with wasi-sdk (Dockerfile.wasi-sdk); the prebuilt .wasm files are checked in and run by Wasmtime's benchmarking. WAMR tests/benchmarks/sightglass builds an older subset (not verified).
claims_to_verify: WAMR's Sightglass subset

picks.name: PolyBench/C 4.2.1
picks.what: 30 static-control-flow numerical kernels (BLAS-like, solvers, stencils, data mining, dynamic programming), each about 100-200 lines. Ohio State University BSD-style license.
picks.size: About 6.8k lines across 64 .c/.h files: 30 kernels plus utilities/polybench.c (about 550 lines). Not re-measured.
picks.why_good: The most-used C suite in wasm performance research. Its FP loop nests test -O0 vs -O2 FP equivalence and array indexing, and each kernel plus a stub fits in one TU.
picks.blockers:
Replace utilities/polybench.c, which references posix_memalign, calloc/free, printf, gettimeofday (under POLYBENCH_TIME), sched_setscheduler and exit. The stub defines polybench_alloc_data over a static arena and also defines free, because each kernel's main frees its arrays through POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY.
print_array's fprintf(stderr) and the strcmp in polybench_prevent_dce never run, but they are still referenced, and a referenced variadic call is a Phase 1 error. On UCRT, stderr also expands to a __acrt_iob_func call. Shim the whole fprintf expression and strcmp with macros.
Do not define POLYBENCH_DUMP_ARRAYS (it removes the guard) or POLYBENCH_USE_C99_PROTO (it adds VLA parameter types).
The default dataset is LARGE. Prefer MINI (0.5-26.5 KB of arrays for the double kernels, the largest being ludcmp at 26,560 B; deriche 64 KB) or SMALL (up to about 233 KB; deriche 384 KB). -DPOLYBENCH_STACK_ARRAYS would put the arrays in a localloc frame, so keep heap mode on the arena.
libm: correlation, cholesky and gramschmidt call sqrt, and deriche calls expf and powf (its default type is float); all are Phase 1 imports. Print a checksum of the live-out arrays, and compile both sides with -ffp-contract=off.
picks.tests: No golden outputs. A checksum of the live-out arrays, compared with native.
picks.wasm_precedent: Not individually verified: 'Not So Fast' (Jangda et al., USENIX ATC 2019); WAMR tests/benchmarks/polybench; the llvm-test-suite copy compiled by WarpDiff; Twine and WaTZ.
claims_to_verify: the line and file counts
the listed wasm research uses

picks.name: TACLeBench
picks.what: Worst-case-execution-time benchmark collection: self-contained C programs in bench/{kernel,sequential,app,parallel,test}. Licenses are mixed and set per benchmark (LGPL, GPL, permissive, RSA terms, and others).
picks.size: Master has 60 benchmarks: kernel 29, sequential 23, app 2, test 3, parallel 3. The WCET 2016 paper described V1.9 with 53. Each benchmark is one to a few files.
picks.why_good: Its paper's abstract describes the programs as free of standard-library and OS dependencies, which makes this the best Phase 1 fit on the list. It mixes FP (fft, ludcmp, minver, cosf), recursion (fac, recursion, quicksort) and integer kernels (md5, sha, bitcount).
picks.blockers:
kernel, sequential, app and test have no system #include and no libc calls; math goes to bundled implementations such as fmref's wcclibm.h.
Single-file kernels run as they are. 8 of the 29 kernels are multi-file (bitcount, cosf, cubic, fft, isqrt, pm, quicksort, sha) and, like the multi-file sequential and app programs, need a one-TU #include wrapper or Phase 2. sha declares printf but never calls it.
parallel/ is different:
- rosace is split into thread1-thread5 folders and uses no threads (stdlib.h/stdint.h plus sqrt/pow/sin/atan, all Phase 1 imports).
- DEBIE needs printf/memcpy/exit (Phase 3).
- PapaBench needs AVR arch/io*.h headers, so exclude it.
picks.tests: main() returns a computed value; compare the exit code with a native build.
picks.wasm_precedent: None found.
claims_to_verify: one-TU wrappers for the multi-file programs compile without static-name collisions

picks.name: Embench-IoT
picks.what: Real embedded programs (from BEEBS) written for bare-metal IoT-class CPUs with no OS and no output stream. Mostly GPL-3.0-or-later; depthconv is Apache-2.0, and md5sum and tarfind are MIT.
picks.size: master src/ has 19 programs: aha-mont64, crc32, depthconv, edn, huffbench, matmult-int, md5sum, nettle-aes, nettle-sha256, nsichneu, picojpeg, qrduino, sglib-combined, slre, statemate, tarfind, ud, wikisort, xgboost. Each has 1-3 .c files (picojpeg 2, qrduino 3, xgboost 2).
picks.why_good: Self-verifying real embedded programs (main returns !correct) with a static heap and no printf. They range from huge branchy state machines (nsichneu, statemate) to pointer-heavy sorting (wikisort, sglib), integer DSP (picojpeg) and nettle crypto.
picks.blockers:
support/main.c and beebsc.h use no libc, and malloc_beebs is a bump allocator over a static heap (it uses only memset).
The harness supplies config.h (CPU_MHZ) and boardsupport.h, which support.h includes, plus stub initialise_board/start_trigger/stop_trigger. Board files normally come from examples/<arch>/<board>/boardsupport.c via support/board.c.
Define these in the harness, since C has no spelling for the explicit import attribute yet:
- memcmp, called in the verify step of 9 benchmarks (edn, huffbench, matmult-int, picojpeg, qrduino, sglib-combined, slre, ud, wikisort)
- slre's strchr, strlen, isdigit, isspace, isxdigit and tolower, without including ctype.h (glibc's macros call __ctype_b_loc)
- qrduino's strlen (qrencode.c:200)
- abort, for nettle-sha256
wikisort calls sqrt, a Phase 1 import, and the float compare macros use fabs/fabsf (intrinsics). md5sum's and nsichneu's printf calls compile only with DEBUG/ROUNDS/DO_TRACING. Multi-file programs need a one-TU wrapper or Phase 2.
picks.tests: Self-verifying: exit 0 means pass.
picks.wasm_precedent: None found.
claims_to_verify: one-TU wrappers for picojpeg, qrduino and xgboost compile without collisions

picks.name: llvm-test-suite SingleSource/Benchmarks (C subset), then UnitTests/MultiSource

SingleSource/UnitTests, Regression/C and MultiSource follow in later phases. License: Apache-2.0 with LLVM Exceptions plus the legacy NCSA license, with third-party notices for Dhrystone, Misc and SmallPT.

CRuby / ruby.wasm: the conservative GC scans the machine stack and registers for VALUEs, but C locals held in IL locals are invisible to that scan. It would need an Asyncify-like spill-to-shadow-stack mode the design does not have, plus fiber context switching. Revisit only if such a mode is added
mruby: overlaps Lua (setjmp errors, computed-goto VM), and its build needs a host Ruby plus rake
Duktape: overlaps QuickJS and Lua (a setjmp-based single-file engine); its test runner is Linux/Node-only
Wren: overlaps Lua (Phase 3: sprintf plus va_list, computed goto)
zForth: needs setjmp (Phase 3) and has no test suite; Lua covers the interpreter pattern

Redis/Valkey: the server needs fork (BGSAVE), sockets/epoll, threads and signals, which a pure-IL assembly will not have. Redis 8 is RSALv2/SSPL/AGPL. Only its data-structure files (sds, dict, listpack) could be lifted later
BusyBox: fork/exec, signals, termios and a Kconfig host build, which we will never have; the pure applets duplicate zlib/bzip2 coverage
libgit2: filesystem- and mmap-heavy and needs fixture repositories; little compiler-feature value per line compared with SQLite
Quake (quakegeneric/WinQuake): its README reportedly says it only compiles for 32-bit architectures, and the MSIL triples are 64-bit; doomgeneric covers the game-engine slot
eSpeak NG: GPL, and needs its compiled data files at run time through fopen (Phase 3); lower value than Opus/minimp3
GLPK: GPL, with variadic definitions and MathProg setjmp (Phase 3). FP-solver coverage comes from PolyBench, Box2D and Graphviz
GSL: 1,373 files (Phase 2/3); FP coverage comes from PolyBench and musl libm
FFTW 3: the git repo lacks the generated codelets (they need the OCaml genfft), and a release has about 3,000 files; KISS FFT covers FFT in Phase 1

libjpeg-turbo: Phase 3 (setjmp in TurboJPEG and the tools, snprintf in jerror.c) with SIMD on by default. If a Phase 1 image decoder is wanted, stb_image (STBI_NO_SIMD, STBI_NO_THREAD_LOCALS, arena malloc) is the better alternate
libpng: default error handling is setjmp, and it adds little beyond zlib, which it needs; revisit in Phase 3
FLAC and libvorbis/libogg: overlap Opus and minimp3. libvorbis uses alloca at 56 sites (Phase 3), and FLAC selects x86 SIMD through cpuid inline asm
Xiph/mpg123 audio-decoder bundle: split up. Opus is picked, minimp3 covers MP3, and libmpg123 (LGPL) overlaps
xz/liblzma: overlaps zlib/bzip2/zstd, and its x86 CLMUL/asm paths turn on under the x86_64 predefines. If it is ever added, avoid the backdoored 5.6.0/5.6.1 releases
cmark: overlaps md4c, and its renderers need snprintf (Phase 3)
libyaml: overlaps md4c and Expat as a parser test, and its emitter needs sprintf
cJSON: needs sprintf, sscanf and strtod even with hooks (Phase 3); jsmn covers JSON in Phase 1
miniz: overlaps zlib and tinf
heatshrink and FastLZ: overlap LZ4, LZAV and tinf, with no wasm precedent
QOI: no wasm precedent and overlaps the other codec picks (an easy add later)
tiny-AES-c, SipHash, B-Con crypto-algorithms and tiny_sha3: overlap Monocypher, BLAKE2 and TweetNaCl, with no wasm precedent
BLAKE3 C: overlaps BLAKE2, and blake3_dispatch.c may compile CPUID detection under __x86_64__
BearSSL: hundreds of files and no wasm precedent, and it needs BR_* configuration to avoid x86 intrinsics and __int128. libsodium and Monocypher cover crypto
xxHash: overlaps zstd, which embeds XXH64; a good alternate with XXH_VECTOR=XXH_SCALAR and XXH_NO_STDLIB
Ryu: the library is C, but its tests are C++ (gtest/Bazel) and no wasm use was verified. musl libm and SoftFloat cover bit-level FP; a good alternate with RYU_ONLY_64_BIT_OPS
stb_image, stb_truetype and stb_vorbis: Phase 1 alternates (with STBI_NO_SIMD, STBI_NO_THREAD_LOCALS and arena macros), left out to keep the tiers small; stb_sprintf is picked
Argon2 reference (JetStream argon2-wasm): Monocypher already includes Argon2, and JetStream builds opt.c with SIMD
TSF (JetStream tsf-wasm): Phase 2/3 (stdio files, variadics), low value
JetStream quicksort.c and float-mm.c: covered by Sightglass quicksort, PolyBench and the Stanford programs in llvm-test-suite
Dhrystone 2.1, Whetstone, LINPACK: no real self-check; copies with reference outputs come with the llvm-test-suite pick
STREAM: mostly printf output and timing, plus about 240 MB of static arrays at the default size; keep in mind as a later data-segment stress test
wasm3 mandelbrot and C-Ray: stdio output and argv parsing. mandel's long double math runs as double on MSIL, so it differs from a native x86_fp80 build
Computer Language Benchmarks Game: overlaps the llvm-test-suite BenchmarkGame and the Sightglass shootout, and most variants need threads, SIMD, GMP or PCRE
Ostrich: Phase 3 (getopt_long, printf), a small wasm-research footprint, and overlaps PolyBench
MiBench: multi-file with file inputs (Phase 2/3); a copy is in llvm-test-suite MultiSource, which the llvm-test-suite pick covers
llvm-test-suite UnitTests/Regression/MultiSource: folded into the llvm-test-suite pick as its Phase 2-4 follow-up (Regression/C also carries the gcc-c-torture copy with skip lists)
Emscripten benchmark suite (C programs): folded into the Emscripten corpus pick

PCRE2: overlaps Oniguruma, which was picked for its vscode-oniguruma wasm use. But Oniguruma's upstream ended in April 2025, so PCRE2 (without JIT) is the first replacement if a maintained regex engine is wanted

checks.correction: The definition in the TU wins. Direct calls bind to the module's method, and so do SelectionDAG library calls (for example llvm.sqrt to sqrt) whose IL name matches a defined function.
